extracted.intended_audience: actors, playwrights, and authors; literate readers of The Spectator interested in theatrical performance and authorial conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and standards for theatrical performance (gesture, countenance, voice, audience management) together with norms for authorship and publication (use of fictitious letters, crediting sources, honesty in what is sold to readers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Govern the countenance with judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: As the Countenance admits of so great Variety, it requires also great Judgment to govern it. Not that the Form of the Face is to be shifted on every Occasion, lest it turn to Farce and Buffoonery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not change the face on every occasion; exercise judgment so expressions suit the occasion and avoid overacting that becomes farce or buffoonery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the eyes to mark emotions appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: The Eyes have a wonderful Power of marking the Emotions of the Mind, sometimes by a stedfast Look, sometimes by a careless one, now by a sudden Regard, then by a joyful Sparkling, as the Sense of the Words is diversified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary eye-expression (steadfast, careless, sudden regard, joyful sparkle) in step with the meaning of the words to communicate emotion subtly and effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let action conform to the sentiments of the soul
rubrics_metrics.description: Action is, as it were, the Speech of the Features and Limbs, and must therefore conform itself always to the Sentiments of the Soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure gestures and bodily action are true manifestations of inner feeling; gesture should match and express the speaker's sentiments rather than contradict them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use action as a universal language
rubrics_metrics.description: Action is a kind of Universal Tongue; all Men are subject to the same Passions, and consequently know the same Marks of them in others, by which they themselves express them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on physical action to communicate to audiences of varied understanding—gesture conveys passion where words may fail or be misunderstood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good sense is essential to a good player
rubrics_metrics.description: Without Good Sense no one can be a good Player, and that he is very unfit to personate the Dignity of a Roman Hero, who cannot enter into the Rules for Pronunciation and Gesture delivered by a Roman Orator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors must possess good judgment and understand principles of pronunciation and gesture (as taught by classical orators) to convincingly portray dignified roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch and modulate the voice within its natural compass
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Voice ... has its particular Medium and Compass, and the Sweetness of Speech consists in leading it through all the Variety of Tones naturally, and without touching any Extreme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find the natural pitch and compass of your voice and lead it through varied tones without extreme reaches; anecdote: Gracchus used an ivory pipe to find pitch—'Leave the Pipe at home, but carry the Sense of this Custom with you.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Action, show, and dress are allowable when they enhance entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Advantages of Action, Show, and Dress on these Occasions are allowable, because the Merit consists in being capable of imposing upon us to our Advantage and Entertainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scenic embellishments are permissible if they serve to impose upon the audience beneficially—i.e., to enhance understanding, emotion, or enjoyment rather than merely to dazzle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actors should cultivate techniques to win the audience's affections
rubrics_metrics.description: The manner of taking an Audience, and laying wait not only for their superficial Applause, but also for insinuating into their Affections and Passions, by the artful Management of the Look, Voice, and Gesture of the Speaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate use of look, voice, and gesture can be used strategically to move the audience beyond superficial applause to genuine emotional engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of fictitious letters and personae is a legitimate literary device
rubrics_metrics.description: I often chuse this way of casting my Thoughts into a Letter ... First, out of the Policy of those who try their Jest upon another, before they own it themselves. Secondly, because I would extort a little Praise ... Thirdly, because it gave me an Opportunity of introducing a great variety of Characters ... Fourthly, because the Dignity Spectatorial would have suffered ... And lastly, because they often serve to bring in, more naturally, such additional Reflections as have been placed at the End of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorial adoption of fictitious correspondents or names can: test jokes anonymously, attract praise otherwise withheld, introduce varied characters, preserve the narrator's dignity, and facilitate natural transitions to reflective commentary. It is an intentional and defensible compositional tactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should signal what is truth and what is fiction in their writing
rubrics_metrics.description: I think the most ordinary Reader may be able to discover, by my way of writing, what I deliver in these Occurrences as Truth, and what as Fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stylistic cues so that readers can tell when an account is factual versus fictional or allegorical; treat each paper as a distinct tract independent of others to avoid confusion about veracity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers may legitimately vary between diverting and serious aims
rubrics_metrics.description: There are some who affirm a Paper of this Nature should always turn upon diverting Subjects, and others who find Fault with every one of them that hath not an immediate Tendency to the Advancement of Religion or Learning ... since I see one half of my Conduct patronized by each side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An essay periodical may alternate between entertainment and instruction; the author should ensure writings are innocent at least and aimed to discountenance vice and support wisdom and virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty of an author: disclose borrowings and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: He ought to own all that he had borrowed from others, and lay in a clear light all that he gives his Spectators for their Money, with an Account of the first Manufacturers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should acknowledge translations, quotations, and borrowings instead of passing them off as wholly original; provide clear attribution so readers know the provenance of material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial and literary fair-dealing: disclose exceptions and avoid cheating
rubrics_metrics.description: The Philosopher made it a Rule of Trade, that your Profit ought to be the common Profit; and it is unjust to make any Step towards Gain, wherein the Gain of even those to whom you sell is not also consulted ... he is no better than a Cheat who sells any thing without telling the Exceptions against it, as well as what is to be said to its Advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether in trade or in selling words to readers, one must reveal both the advantages and the exceptions/limitations of what is offered; profit should not be pursued at the buyer's expense.
